artifact: CP1 - PRE-REGISTRATION. Written BEFORE any of the 19 cities' law was read. This file fixes, in advance, what reading would put each city in each class, so that a result can be recognised as confirming or contradicting the plan rather than being fitted to it after the fact.

whyThisIsARegistrationAndNotANote: The classes are irreversibly load-bearing: setbackCellMayBeMoved releases only `unaccounted` cells, so a wrong (b) freezes a fabricated line onto real parcels. A hypothesis held loosely is not an acceptable input.

The first lane's own failure mode was a search that returned a DIFFERENT CITY (mart/crawford/creedmoor). Pre-registering the admissibility rule before searching is what makes a wrong-city hit visible as a violation of a stated rule rather than a plausible-looking answer.

theRuleBeingApplied.source: _decisions/2026-09-18_phase0_closeout_rulings.md, Ruling 5 as amended by A-224 (operator, 2026-09-18 about 17:55Z)
theRuleBeingApplied.quote: the lane classifies each of the 40 cities at source: (a) a zoned city whose layer we never acquired gets a declared refusal naming the city ... (b) an unzoned city whose ordinance sets a city-wide line gets the default row with its plat disclosure (Gholson first, per OT-10); (c) an unzoned city with no city-wide line, read at source, gets a checked absence naming what was read.
theRuleBeingApplied.a: zoned - the city's own law establishes zoning districts (a district-establishment section, an enumerated district list, or an adopted official zoning map with an ordinance establishing districts). The layer was never acquired. Class (a) does NOT require a tractable acquisition; it is a statement about the city's law.
theRuleBeingApplied.b: unzoned - no districts in the city's own law, but that law sets a city-wide setback line (a front/rear/side line applying to buildings generally, with no district qualifier).
theRuleBeingApplied.c: unzoned - the city's own law sets no city-wide line AND establishes no districts. A positive read that produces this shape is what class (c) requires.
theRuleBeingApplied.unclassified: the city's own law could not be read. Legitimate, and preferred over inference. Never written as refused or absent-verified.

admissibilityRule_reRegisteredFromTheFir.rule: A source is admissible only if it names the city AND the correct Texas county, or is the city's own official site carrying a Texas address. A .gov/.us/.org domain is NOT sufficient.
admissibilityRule_reRegisteredFromTheFir.why: cityofcreedmoor.org is Creedmoor, NORTH CAROLINA and the Crawford NE revize site is Crawford, NEBRASKA. Both look official. Mart, TX returns Martindale, TX - same state, neighbouring county, no state mismatch to catch it.
operationalTests: the retrieved text must name the city and a Texas county, or the address/phone in it must be in the right county
any highway, agency acronym or zip in the text that belongs to another state is a hard reject
a search-result SUMMARY is never a source of law (first lane's DEAD-END, restated)

preRegisteredDecisionRule_perCity._reading: For each city: the reading that would make it (a); the reading that would make it (b); the reading that would make it (c); and what would leave it unclassified. Parcels are P-326's counts as restated by the dispatch; counties are the dispatch's where given and my expectation where marked (verify at source; not asserted as fact here).

preRegisteredReadPlan.order: thrall first (highest value: only row that can move a class away from (a)), then the five remaining unresolved, then the thirteen by descending parcels
preRegisteredReadPlan.perCity: find the city's own code host (municode / ecode360 / amlegal / codepublishing / the city's own site), open the zoning or subdivision chapter, read the district-establishment and dimensional-standards sections
recordPerRow: a quote carrying the decisive text
gradeVocabulary: call (who/when/what was said, marked as such)

whatWouldFalsifyThisPlan: A city producing a (b) row from a source that does not set a line applying to buildings generally (e.g. a line attached only to a specific use, a subdivision plat, or a manufactured-home placement rule) - that is (c), not (b).
A city producing an (a) row on the strength of a planning commission, a comprehensive plan, a real-estate field, or a parcel's district code - none of those is a district established in law.
Any row whose cited source turns out to name a different city, county or state.
whatThisLaneWillNotDo: classify a city it could not read at source
